Article Title: 'Step beyond books to connect with children': PM Modi's message on Teachers' Day
Article Text:
PM Modi meets National Teachers Awards winners

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged teachers to “step beyond textbooks” to ensure that children do not lose out on their childhood.The prime minister's message came during his interaction with recipients of the National Teachers’ Awards at his residence on Friday, a day ahead of Teachers’ Day, which commemorates the birth anniversary of former President and renowned educationist Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan."We need to step outside of books and the syllabus much more than before and get into the lives of children. Childhood shouldn't be allowed to die. And the biggest task of keeping childhood alive can be done by a teacher. It's the teacher's job to ensure the child within remains," he said.To drive home his point, PM Modi cited growing screen addiction among children, particularly their increasing dependence on video games. He also flagged drug consumption as a concern, saying the problem was no longer confined to universities or major cities."Screen time has now become a form of addiction. A thought occurs to me: if a child begins to take a keen interest in sports, and by sports, I don't mean video games but actually playing on the field. Then slowly, they can come out of it. And we should make it a habit to involve kids as much as possible in creativity, and we should design some programmes for that," the prime minister said."Now take the case of drugs. It's not just in big cities or universities anymore, nobody even knows what it is; someone just comes and gives it. Teachers should watch for behavioural changes in children," he added.Saturday marks the 138th birth anniversary of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who also served as Vice President of India. Later in the day, PM Modi will visit Shri Ram College of Commerce, which is celebrating its centenary.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi urges teachers to ensure children do not lose out on their childhood. He cites growing screen addiction among children, particularly their dependence on video games. Saturday marks the 138th birth anniversary of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who served as Vice President of India.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi vs C Joseph Vijay: Can TVK chief do what Arvind Kejriwal could not?
Article Text:
Vijay's national ambitions: Can the TVK chief succeed where Kejriwal failed?

Vijay's extraordinary first step

Vijay emerged as the disrupter-in-chief in Tamil Nadu elections.

Congress leader on TVK's 'Vijay-for-PM' pitch.

The 'agnipath' of Vijay's path

Rahul Gandhi's political journey.

Can Tamil Nadu be Vijay’s launchpad?

BJP has used the opportunity to question TVK-Congress alliance.

Why Congress cannot simply step aside

The Kejriwal test

Vijay's one-point lead on Kejriwal

The honeymoon period between Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and its coalition partner, the Congress, appears to be over. Barely months after the two parties came together to form the government, they are already sparring over a question that is ostensibly about the 2029 Lok Sabha election: Who should be the opposition's prime ministerial face - Rahul Gandhi or Vijay?What began as statements and counter-statements between the two party leaders has quickly acquired a sharper political edge.TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna pitched Vijay as a potential national leader, arguing that the country's highest political office should go to a leader from Tamil Nadu. On the other hand, state minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the Tamil Nadu cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the PM candidate in 2029.The confrontation spilled into the assembly as well. Congress Legislature Party leader and MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted on August 31 from the section allotted to TVK legislators to the front row of the opposition benches.But beneath the immediate fight over Rahul versus Vijay lies a much bigger question: Does Vijay intend to remain a powerful Tamil Nadu leader, or does he see the state's 2026 mandate as the launchpad for a national political project?And if the latter is the plan, can he succeed where Arvind Kejriwal could not?The scale of Vijay's rise explains why the 2029 debate has surfaced so early.The April 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly election ended nearly six decades of dominance by the DMK and AIADMK.TVK, only two years old, emerged as the largest party with 108 seats in the 234-member assembly. The DMK won 59 and AIADMK 47, while Congress secured five seats, with the remaining seats going to smaller allies.TVK was therefore not merely a new party that performed better than expected. It emerged as the central political force in an election that disrupted the state's traditional two-party equilibrium.There was, however, one problem: 108 seats were still short of the 118 required for a simple majority.That made Congress indispensable.Vijay eventually formed the government with the support of MLAs from Congress [5], VCK [2] and IUML [2], along with outside support from the Left parties [4]. The MDMK, which has two MLAs, later extended its support.Congress moved away from its long-standing association with the DMK and backed a TVK-led government along with smaller allies, taking the coalition's strength to 121. Vijay was sworn in as CM on May 10.Congress had submitted its letter of support after the election, making it clear that its support would be conditional on TVK keeping "communal forces" out of the alliance.The 234-member assembly currently has seven vacancies following the resignation of six AIADMK MLAs and Vijay vacating his second seat, Trichy East. The effective strength of the House is therefore 227, bringing the majority mark down to 114.The political equation is unusual. Congress is the junior partner, with only five seats, but its support helped Vijay cross the majority mark. At the same time, TVK's 108 seats give Vijay overwhelming dominance within the coalition.That inversion may be at the heart of the present tension.Congress had been with the DMK in the pre-poll alliance and had never secured a place in MK Stalin's cabinet. After the results, however, it quickly moved to TVK's side and helped Vijay form the government.The alliance therefore contains a built-in contradiction: the party that needs Vijay's government to survive does not want Vijay to emerge as the leader of the national opposition.Vijay's route to Delhi runs into a problem that no amount of success in Tamil Nadu can entirely solve: numbers.Tamil Nadu sends 39 MPs to the Lok Sabha. Even a TVK sweep in 2029 would leave Vijay nowhere close to the 272 seats needed for a majority in the 543-member House.History, however, offers a little hope.In the past, India has had PMs whose parties did not come close to a Lok Sabha majority. HD Deve Gowda became PM in 1996 after the Janata Dal won just 46 seats, emerging as the consensus choice of the United Front with Congress support. IK Gujral followed a year later under much the same arrangement, with the Janata Dal holding only around 45 seats. Chandra Shekhar became prime minister in 1990 after breaking away from the Janata Dal with just 64 MPs, relying on outside support from Congress.This may give Vijay some hope.But it is also where the historical comparison begins to fray. The coalition politics that made these leaders PMs belonged to a different national landscape where coalition governments were a norm. The BJP, however, has changed that equation, building the NDA into a durable national coalition rather than the loose, post-election arrangements that defined much of the 1990s.The opposition, meanwhile, has come together in the form of the INDIA bloc which Vijay's TVK is not part of yet.And yet, paradoxically, being outside the INDIA bloc may give Vijay an advantage over Rahul Gandhi.Rahul comes with the weight of the Congress's history: its national footprint, its alliances and rivalries, the Nehru-Gandhi legacy and the political resistance that the party can provoke among regional leaders. Vijay comes with much less baggage. He would enter a coalition conversation not as the leader of a decades-old national party, but as a new political force with a mass following built before he entered politics.That distinction could matter if the next Lok Sabha produces another fractured mandate. But that is a big if, and one that looks unlikely in the present circumstances.Congress MP Karti Chidambaram has already put the arithmetic bluntly: "Every party has dreams, ambitions, and desires ... but we know what the political reality is. There are 543 constituencies."Thus, for Vijay, even if his party manages to sweep all 39 Tamil Nadu seats, the real test would be in finding enough allies to make Delhi possible.There is, however, one route Vijay could attempt that would give his national project a distinct political identity.He could build around Tamil Nadu's distinctive relationship with the Centre and a broader southern assertion in national politics — the argument that Delhi needs a stronger voice from a region that has historically resisted political and cultural centralisation.That could give TVK's national project a political argument beyond Vijay's celebrity and the anti-incumbency against established parties.But it comes with its own problem.A political identity rooted in Tamil pride and southern assertion may work strongly in Tamil Nadu, but it does not automatically translate into votes in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal or other states.Vijay would therefore have to balance two identities: the Tamil leader whose legitimacy comes from Tamil Nadu and the national leader who must persuade voters elsewhere that his politics is not confined to the state.For Congress, the dispute is not simply about Rahul Gandhi's personal ambitions or the future of the Gandhi family. It is about whether the party can retain its position as the principal national pole of the opposition after years of organisational and electoral decline.Rahul has spent years positioning himself as the principal challenger to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP. Congress's improved performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and Rahul's emergence as leader of opposition strengthened that claim.The subsequent assembly elections, however, have weakened the party's position against the BJP.A recent survey placing Rahul as the second-most preferred PM choice and Vijay next is nevertheless significant. Vijay's position is remarkable for a leader whose party has contested only one assembly election, even though such surveys are hardly a substitute for actual elections.For Congress, conceding the national leadership question to Vijay now would risk allowing another regional leader to occupy the political space the party is trying to reclaim, especially after the weakened positioning of Mamata Banerjee, MK Stalin and Kejriwal.Kejriwal also began with an extraordinary political breakthrough in a single territory before attempting to turn his party into a national alternative.When he launched the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in November 2012, his political project was built around challenging established parties, particularly Congress, which had governed Delhi for 15 years under Sheila Dikshit.AAP's breakthrough came almost immediately. Kejriwal became CM in December 2013, resigned after 49 days and returned in February 2015 with one of the most emphatic mandates in Indian electoral politics: AAP won 67 of Delhi's 70 assembly seats, reducing Congress to zero.But Kejriwal did not intend to stop at Delhi.The 2014 Lok Sabha election was his first major attempt to build a national footprint. AAP contested 432 seats and won four, all in Punjab. Kejriwal himself challenged Narendra Modi in Varanasi, while Kumar Vishwas contested Amethi against Rahul Gandhi. Neither challenge produced the national breakthrough AAP was seeking.The party then entered the Punjab and Goa assembly elections in 2017. Punjab became a second political laboratory, with AAP winning 20 of 117 seats and emerging as the principal opposition force behind Congress. Goa, however, exposed the limits of the expansion strategy, with AAP failing to win a single assembly seat.Punjab eventually provided the big breakthrough. In the 2022 election, AAP won 92 of 117 seats and formed a government under Bhagwant Mann.Kejriwal had therefore achieved something genuinely difficult: he had built governments in two states and turned AAP into a recognisable political force beyond Delhi.Yet the national leap remained elusive.AAP's electoral strength outside its core states never matched the scale of its Delhi and Punjab victories. In Gujarat, where it tried to establish itself as a third force, the party won five assembly seats in 2022, while Goa remained marginal. Its Lok Sabha presence also remained modest.The Tamil Nadu CM has one advantage over Kejriwal though that their starting points are different.Kejriwal had to build a mass political identity almost from scratch. Vijay, however, spent decades building one through cinema before entering politics. He then converted that popularity into 108 assembly seats in his very first election, which was dubbed as an extraordinary political conversion.But it can also become a weakness.The question is no longer whether millions of people know Vijay. They do.The question is whether voters who know him as an actor and Tamil Nadu CM will vote for TVK in states where the party has no political history, local leadership or cadre network.To go national, Vijay would need candidates, local leaders, a cadre network and alliances. Most importantly, he would need a political proposition that resonates with voters who do not know him primarily as a Tamil film star.This is where Kejriwal's experience matters most.AAP's success in Delhi could not simply be reproduced across the country. Punjab offered a favourable political opening, but Goa and Gujarat demonstrated that national visibility and electoral organisation are very different things.Vijay's task could be even harder because many of the states he would need to enter already have powerful regional leaders with their own political ambitions.For now, the 2029 PM debate may therefore be premature, but the political conflict it has exposed is not. Vijay may need Congress to consolidate the power he has won in Tamil Nadu even as he seeks to challenge Congress's claim to national opposition leadership.That is the paradox at the heart of his political project.If Vijay can use the Congress alliance to build a durable organisation without becoming politically dependent on it, he may have found a route Kejriwal could not. But if TVK's national ambitions remain ahead of its organisational reach, the 2029 debate could end up looking less like the beginning of a national challenge and more like the first sign of a regional party reaching beyond its electoral weight.
Article Summary: Vijay emerged as the disrupter-in-chief in Tamil Nadu elections. Congress is the junior partner, with only five seats, but its support helped Vijay cross the majority mark. At the same time, TVK seats give Vijay overwhelming dominance within the coalition.

Article Title: Air India Phuket-Delhi incident: All 3 hydraulic systems failed; pilot tested positive for psychoactive substance
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

MUMBAI: The preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet, triggering an autopilot disengagement, stall warning and an altitude upset. Alongside the technical findings, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has recommended that the DGCA take action against the Pilot-in-Command, who tested non-negative for psychoactive substance use following the flight."The confirmation of use of psycho-active substance is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority," the report said. The interim safety recommendation asked the regulator to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psycho-active substance." Post-flight, both pilots underwent a breath analyser test, which came back satisfactory. But the subsequent psychoactive substance detection test returned a non-negative result for the PIC, a finding confirmed by a follow-up laboratory blood test. The co-pilot tested negative on both counts.The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window.VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region. At 04:02:43 UTC, the flight control system "detected loss of green hydraulic system." Four seconds later, the flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of Blue and Yellow hydraulic systems. With all three systems compromised simultaneously, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet from its assigned level, the report said.The co-pilot, who was Pilot Flying, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift. "At around 04:02:52 UTC, the Blue hydraulic system was recovered, and a few seconds later, the Yellow hydraulic and the Green hydraulic systems were also recovered," the report said. It restored normal flight control surfaces within seconds of the failure.But with seatbelt signs off during cruise, the sudden upset threw passengers and crew around the cabin. Twenty-four people, including four cabin crew, needed medical attention on landing; four were hospitalised with serious injuries. The cabin damage was extensive: cracked ceiling panels across multiple rows, dislodged overhead bins, a broken emergency exit handle, a lavatory commode "uprooted from its original location," and a bent crew seat. Despite the injuries, the flight crew chose not to divert, opting instead to continue to Delhi while requesting medical priority from ATC. The aircraft landed safely on runway 11L at 05:30 UTC, around ninety minutes after the failure.Investigators have already flagged one detail for closer scrutiny: the aircraft was dispatched from Phuket under an active Minimum Equipment List item for the Power Transfer Unit, invoked a week earlier on July 28. The PTU serves as an auxiliary hydraulic source shared between the green and yellow systems, and its status at the time of the failure is expected to be a focus of the ongoing probe. Flight recorder data has been downloaded and is under analysis, and a technical team from Airbus and France's BEA inspected the aircraft in Delhi in mid-August, after which hydraulic components and fluid samples were removed for further testing.“The Airbus A320 aircraft has three hydraulic systems. They are identified as the green, blue and yellow systems. Together they supply hydraulic power at 3000 psi (206 bar) to the main power users. Services which are not used during flight are isolated from the main supply. Hydraulic fluid cannot be transferred from one system to another. Each system has its own hydraulic reservoir,” the report said, explaining the hydraulics on the aircraft.On the green system, the normal source of pressure is the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) located on the left engine and, as an auxiliary source, the Power Transfer Unit (PTU). On the blue system, the normal source of pressure is the electrical pump (E-Pump) and, as an auxiliary source, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT). On the yellow system, the normal source of pressure is the EDP located on the right engine and as auxiliary sources the PTU and the electric pump (E-Pump). “Each hydraulic system pressurisation information is available for the aircraft systems through one pressure transmitter (numerical value of the pressure), two pressure switches (discrete value indicating if there is a loss of pressure). Relevant Hydraulic components were removed from the aircraft for further analysis,” the report said. The PTU is an auxiliary pressure supply for either the green or yellow systems without transfer of fluid between the two systems. It operates automatically if there is a delta pressure of 500 psi between the green/yellow or yellow/green hydraulic systems, it addedThe said report is preliminary, and a detailed technical investigation is still underway.
Article Summary: Preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet. Autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet.

Article Text:

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday congratulated his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni, a day after she become Italy's longest continuously serving prime minister since the post- World War II era.In a post on X, PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni."Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership," the prime minister wrote."Her friendship has also been instrumental in advancing the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership and I look forward to continuing our close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of our countries. My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead," he added.The two leaders' widely known friendship is often referred to as "Melodi" - a combination of their surnames.Meloni, who has served as Italy's prime minister since October 2022, is the first woman to hold that position.On Thursday, her conservative administration marked 1,413 uninterrupted days in office, making it Italy's longest-serving continuous government since World War II and surpassing the record previously set by late former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi from 2001 to 2005.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi congratulates Italian PM Giorgia Meloni on her 1,413 days in office. PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni. Meloni has served as Italy's prime minister since October 2022, the first woman to hold that position.

Article Title: Bargaining tactics? Why BJP's 'solo pitch' in Punjab may have message for Akalis
Article Text:
File photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal.

BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh reiterated that the party is preparing to contest all 117 Punjab assembly seats.

BJP's message: We can do it alone

But the doors don't seem completely shut

Akalis have not been subtle about wanting alliance with BJP

Former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal's remarks added to speculation over a possible revival of ties.

Akalis need BJP more than before

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann accused the Akali Dal of seeking a reunion with the BJP for political power.

Why BJP may have kept the door open

But does BJP actually need the Akalis?

Is the BJP playing hardball with the Akalis in Punjab ? Yet another senior BJP leader has announced that the party will contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab on its own strength.BJP national general secretary Satish Poonia, in his first media interaction after being appointed the party's organisational in-charge for Punjab, made it clear that the message from the central leadership was to prepare for all 117 constituencies in the state. He also sought to play down Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month, saying meetings between political leaders should not automatically be read as signs of an alliance.Poonia is not the first senior BJP leader to reiterate the 'solo contest' point.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh had earlier told party functionaries in Punjab that the BJP would contest all 117 assembly seats independently.And yet, the speculation of an alliance between the two parties refuses to go away.The question then is whether the BJP is really shutting the door on its old ally or raising the bar before any possible deal.The BJP today has reasons to sound more confident than it did when both parties went their separate ways.The BJP in Punjab was the junior partner of the Akalis for decades. The arrangement gave the BJP a share of Punjab's urban and Hindu-dominated constituencies while the SAD remained the dominant force in the alliance.In the 2017 assembly election, the last Punjab polls the two parties contested together, the SAD fought 94 seats and the BJP just 23. The BJP won three and the Akalis 15.This arrangement will clearly no longer work for the BJP.Since splitting with the Akalis, the BJP has been working towards a plan. The party has been trying to expand beyond its old pockets in Punjab, in line with its national growth, and build an independent base. The West Bengal victory has indeed strengthened the confidence within the party. Punjab BJP leaders have also publicly argued that the party's improved vote share and national presence have strengthened the case for fighting the elections independently.That makes the repeated declaration of contesting 117 seats more than just a message to the Akalis. It is also a message to BJP workers that the party intends to build its own organisation across Punjab.Interestingly, even in the middle of this high-pitched rhetoric, the Student Organisation of India (SOI), which is the students’ wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal, extended support to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) candidate in the Panjab University Campus Students’ Council elections and helped its candidate win the presidential post.The SOI offered this olive branch to BJP’s student wing a day before the voting and helped ABVP create a record of winning the top post in the students’ council election for the second time in a row.This campus politics bonhomie was significant messaging. The Akalis, who had walked away from the decades-old alliance with the BJP in 2020 over the now-repealed farm bills, have dropped very clear and open hints that they desperately want to revive the ties.There have been a series of overtures from their end to seek an alliance without expressing that in as many words.If the BJP is keeping its cards close to its chest, the Akalis have been far more open about it.The PM Modi-Sukhbir Badal meeting was perhaps the beginning of this outreach. It was their first one-on-one political meeting since the SAD walked out of the BJP-led NDA in 2020 over the three farm laws, ending an alliance that had lasted nearly two decades.Days after this meeting, the SAD reversed its stand on the Delimitation Bill and announced its support for the constitutional amendment bill which the BJP is trying to pass in Parliament. This was a huge U-turn that prompted digs from the ruling AAP and the Congress over the SAD’s desperation for an alliance with the BJP.The shift in stance drew attention because the party had earlier taken a much more critical position on delimitation. The SAD had in April stated in Lok Sabha that the BJP was repeatedly changing the goal post on women's reservation and decried that the delimitation exercise was being conducted in the garb of the Women's Reservation Bill.Then came more signals from within the Akali leadership.Senior Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia went public advocating an alliance, and said that people want SAD and the BJP to come together for peace, development and progress of Punjab.Majithia's statement came after his sister and former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal stoked fresh speculation about a re-alliance between the Akali Dal and the BJP by expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that carried progress to Punjab from Delhi.None of these statements amounted to a formal alliance proposal. However, they made it clear that the Akali leadership was increasingly interested in reviving ties with the BJP.The reason is not difficult to see. The Akalis have been pushed to the fringes of Punjab politics.Its vote share and seat share have declined in the last few elections. In fact, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP managed a huge lead over SAD in terms of vote share.The BJP secured 18.56% of the votes but failed to win a parliamentary seat in Punjab. The Akali Dal, despite winning Bathinda, finished with 13.42% vote share.The BJP also finished ahead of SAD candidates across several constituencies and led in 24 assembly segments. In the 2022 assembly polls, by comparison, the BJP's vote share was only around 6.6%, while SAD was a little over 18%.That perhaps explains why the Akalis seem desperate for an alliance. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has claimed that the Shiromani Akali Dal leadership is "on its knees" to forge an alliance with the BJP and return to power in the state to "loot" it again.So, the big question is: why is the BJP acting tough? Is it against reviving the alliance with the Akalis? Or is the BJP just playing hardball to ensure that it is the “big brother” in any future alliance?For the Akalis, the decline has been much more painful.Akalis, who dominated Punjab politics for years, were reduced to three seats in the 2022 assembly election and one Lok Sabha seat in 2024. Now, the party has to compete not only with the Congress but also with AAP, which swept the last state election, and also a BJP trying to expand independently.That perhaps explains the urgency.When BJP and SAD were in alliance earlier, there was little ambiguity about who was the senior partner.The SAD had more seats and more say in deciding the assembly seats and the chief ministerial candidate. The BJP accepted most terms because the arrangement perhaps gave the BJP a space where its independent visibility was limited.But now, if there is an alliance between the two again, it surely will be on completely different terms.The BJP has spent the years since the split trying to build an identity of its own in Punjab. It has brought leaders from other parties into its fold, expanded its organisation and fielded candidates across the entire state in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.Even in recent weeks, it has continued inducting figures from outside the party as it prepares for the assembly contest.For the BJP, therefore, returning to an arrangement in which it simply receives around 20-odd seats would be difficult. This is perhaps where the bargaining may be happening. Therefore, the real question might just be if the Akalis are willing to accept the changed political reality.There is another reason why the BJP may be keeping the Akalis guessing.Declaring an alliance too early could derail BJP's bid to strengthen its organisation in the state build an independent identity. Keeping the 117-seat option alive allows the BJP to continue expanding and encouraging its cadres.The BJP knows the Akalis are willing to return. There is little reason for the BJP to make any commitment before discussing seats and leadership.The public posturing notwithstanding, the BJP also stands to gain from a possible alliance. The BJP's 18.56% vote share in the Lok Sabha election did not translate into a single seat. This shows that the party did expand its base, but that vote share by itself may not be enough.The Akalis, meanwhile, still have traditional pockets of support. That gives both sides something the other may want.Fighting independently gives it the freedom to contest every region, develop new leaders and try to move beyond its traditional urban base. Even an election in which it improves substantially without forming the government could further that objective. An alliance with SAD could interrupt that process.Also, the Sikh community's identity continues to play an important role in Punjab politics. For the BJP, a renewed alliance with the Akali Dal could help it reach sections of Sikh voters and rural Punjab where the party has traditionally struggled to build a strong independent base.For now, the two sides appear to be speaking in very different registers.The Akalis have repeatedly sent signals that they are willing to reopen the relationship. The BJP is listening but not reacting. For now, all BJP leaders are maintaining that the party is preparing for all 117 seats.Yet the Modi-Sukhbir meeting, the SOI-ABVP cooperation and reports of discussions behind the scenes mean the possibility of an alliance cannot be written off either.It is possible that the BJP means exactly what it says and will go into the election alone. But if the two former allies do eventually come together, it is unlikely to be a return to the partnership that existed before 2020.The fight, therefore, may not just be about whether BJP and SAD become allies again. It may be about who gets to be the 'big brother' this time.
Article Summary: BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh reiterated that the party is preparing to contest all 117 Punjab assembly seats. The BJP in Punjab was the junior partner of the Akalis for decades. The arrangement gave the BJP a share of Punjab's urban and Hindu-dominated constituencies.

Article Title: Work hard, own the world
Article Text:
may there always be enough for everyone.

Nediyon

Ulagalandhaan

“Madiyila Mannavan Eydhum Adialandhaan

Thaaya Dhellam Orungu.”

never underestimate the power of someone who appears unassuming. When the right moment comes, every Vamana may blossom into a Trivikrama.

Last week, I was in London and had a day to myself. I decided to visit the Sherlock Holmes Museum. Sherlock Holmes has always been a favourite character of mine. As is often the case in London, getting to the station, followed by two train rides. It was quite a journey, but entirely worth it.On my return, hunger took over. I was delighted when my host suggested a South Indian restaurant. I asked for a dosa .“Not available.” The only item on the menu was Onam sadhya.Of course, it was Onam.And suddenly, the absence of a dosa seemed like a blessing.A sadhya is not merely a meal. It is a celebration of abundance. Sitting in a corner of London, with thoran, erissery and jackfruit payasam before me, felt less like eating and more like being transported to heaven.Onam celebrates the annual return of King Mahabali to visit his people in Kerala. His reign is remembered as an age of prosperity, equality and generosity. The sadhya seems to embody the spirit of his kingdom:That thought took me to another story—that of Vamana , who became Trivikrama. The image at its core—the three cosmic strides of Vishnu—is much older. In the Rigveda, Vishnu is celebrated as the deity who takes three great steps across the universe. It is interesting that the names Rama and Krishna find little mention in the early scriptures, but Trivikrama is omnipresent; both in scriptures and literature, even in ancient Tamil literature. Sangam works such as Paripadal, Kalithogai and Perumpaanatrupadai evoke Vishnu asor—the One who measured the worlds.There is even an ancient tradition connecting the origin of the River Vaigai with this cosmic act. When Trivikrama raised his foot and pierced the upper worlds, Brahma is said to have washed that divine foot. The sacred water that flowed down towards Earth became associated with the Vaigai. Myth, landscape and poetry became woven together.Early Tamil poetry was deeply conscious of landscape, boundaries and celestial order. A God who could cross the limits of the universe with a single stride was a magnificent poetic image.And Thiruvalluvar, who rarely invokes deities directly, chose precisely this image in the Thirukkural .In the chapter on freedom from laziness, he says in Kural 610:“A king who is completely free from laziness will gain all that wasMeasured by the feet of Trivikrama.”The grandeur of the image is striking. Trivikrama measured the worlds with his feet; Valluvar transforms that into a metaphor for human effort. The energetic can reach whatever vastness the universe may contain. What seems beyond one’s grasp may become attainable when one refuses to be held back by indolence. And there is another thought in this transformation from Vamana to Trivikrama:And perhaps that was the unexpected journey I experienced at London: from Sherlock Holmes to an Onam sadhya, to Mahabali, and from Mahabali to Trivikrama; my friend and I travelled quite a lot for the dosa we didn’t get. My takeaway was; don’t be upset if you don’t get what you wanted: you may end up with much more!
Article Summary: Onam celebrates the annual return of King Mahabali to visit his people in Kerala. His reign is remembered as an age of prosperity, equality and generosity. The sadhya seems to embody the spirit of his kingdom. That thought took me to another story—that of Vamana, who became Trivikrama.

Article Title: SC overturns trial court, HC orders to acquit kidnap-murder accused
Article Text:
Supreme Court freed a man sentenced by lower courts

NEW DELHI: For the third time this week, Supreme Court freed a man sentenced by lower courts - in a kidnapping and murder case in the latest instance - questioning their analysis of evidence, and flagging loopholes in the prosecution theory tying the accused to the crime, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.A man was kidnapped in Telangana in 2012 and his father paid a ransom of Rs 1.5 lakh against a demand of Rs 23 lakh. His body was recovered from a fridge in a flat based on the disclosure of the accused, one of whom died during pendency of trial. A trial court convicted the five other accused. Telangana HC analysed evidence and acquitted four, but convicted one.The Supreme Court said barring the postmortem report indicating strangulation, and finding of the body, there was no substantive evidence to link the accused to the murder.Setting aside conviction and sentence, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said, “That victim died of ‘asphyxia due to smothering, associated with strangulation’, is established by the autopsy report and the dead body was detected, tucked away in a refrigerator inside an apartment. But for these, there is no scrap of evidence, worthy of reliance, to connect the six accused to the murder or even the flat.In another case, a man was accused of luring a boy with snacks to sodomise him. He was convicted by an Ambala court in April 2010 for the March 2007 “crime” of unnatural sex and murder, and given life term. Punjab and Haryana HC in Oct 2022 dismissed the appeal.A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said police failed to conduct DNA test of the semen in the undergarment of the accused to match it with the rectal swab collected from victim’s undergarment. SC said the ‘last seen with’ theory is doubtful and that there were several missing links in the chain of the prosecution case. It acquitted the man, who had served 17 years in prison. The drawing of judicial curtains on the case had unpleasant outcomes: a man lost his young child to a crime which went unpunished, while a man unfairly convicted lost his prime years.In the third case, a murder in Bihar 25 years ago saw a trial court and Patna HC convict six persons. A bench of Justices Pardiwala and Chandran acquitted the convicts saying, “There is complete lack of evidence, and eyewitnesses testimonies do not inspire confidence… The case is not that of faulty investigation but of no probe having been carried out.
Article Summary: A man was kidnapped in Telangana in 2012 and his father paid a ransom of Rs 1.5 lakh against a demand of Rs 23 lakh. The Supreme Court said barring the postmortem report indicating strangulation, and finding of the body, there was no substantive evidence to link the accused to the murder.

Article Title: HC allows 2 'linked' to NEET leak to go for counselling

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has directed National Testing Agency (NTA) to declare within 24 hours the NEET-UG re-examination results of two candidates, whose results were withheld over allegations linking them to the question paper leak. Justice Jasmeet Singh pointed out the candidates had not been named as accused by CBI in its chargesheet.While CBI told the court that it did not make them accused, though they had paid money to get question papers, the judge observed that at this stage, it was just an allegation and "therefore, the petitioners cannot be treated as persons against whom criminal culpability has been established or as having been found guilty of any illegality".The court was hearing the students' plea seeking release of their re-NEET results and permission to participate in the ongoing counselling. The CBI chargesheet named the two petitioners as witnesses, and not accused. NTA, however, issued show-cause notices to them and withheld their results.During the hearing, NTA submitted that it withheld the results after CBI informed it that several candidates had allegedly received or shared the question paper of the May 3 examination.On its part, CBI submitted that the petitioners had received the question paper and had the "mens rea" (intent) to commit the illegality, since money had been paid by them for obtaining the question paper.HC observed that the petitioners were at a "nascent stage of their academic careers", and withholding their results merely on the basis of allegations that were yet to be tested would cause serious prejudice to them."The petitioners ought to be permitted to know their results and, subject to the outcome of the proceedings, participate in the further rounds of counseling conducted by the NTA," Justice Singh said. The order recorded denying them an opportunity to participate in counselling at this stage could result in consequences that may not subsequently be adequately remedied.
Article Summary: Delhi HC has directed National Testing Agency (NTA) to declare within 24 hours the NEET-UG re-examination results of two candidates. Results were withheld over allegations linking them to the question paper leak. The court was hearing the students' plea seeking release of their re-NEET results.

Article Title: Chiefs' billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt refuses to follow the family script as she builds her own empire
Article Text:
Gracie Hunt is carving out her own identity beyond the Chiefs

Gracie Hunt’s fashion and philanthropy ventures stand on their own

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Being born into NFL royalty can open almost every door, but it can also make it difficult to prove that you belong in the room for your own reasons. Gracie Hunt knows that tension well. As the daughter of Kansas City Chiefs chairman and CEO Clark Hunt and granddaughter of franchise founder Lamar Hunt, football has always surrounded her. Yet her ambitions have grown far beyond the family business.Hunt could easily have made the Chiefs her entire professional world. Instead, she has built a portfolio that reflects interests she developed long before stepping into the family spotlight.Her journey began with soccer. As a child, she dreamed of following in the footsteps of Mia Hamm and even played the sport through high school. Her family connection to soccer ran deep, too, with her grandfather playing a role in bringing Major League Soccer to the United States.That dream changed after she suffered several concussions. Rather than allowing the setback to define her, Hunt found another competitive outlet in pageantry. She eventually won Miss Kansas USA in 2021, following an example set by her mother, Tavia Hunt, who won the same title in 1993.Her career since then has blended sports, fashion, philanthropy and advocacy. She has worked with the Chiefs Women’s Organization, supported community initiatives and explored opportunities that exist outside the football franchise."The things that have been really important to me my whole life have been faith, family, football and philanthropy," Gracie says. "Because I've always been raised with the mantra that, 'To whom much is given, much is expected'."That philosophy has helped shape the way she views her position. For Hunt, having access to the Chiefs is not necessarily a reason to claim ownership of its spotlight."When it comes to the Chiefs, there's no 'I' in 'team'. It's not about me," Gracie makes clear.One of Hunt’s clearest efforts to establish an independent identity came through fashion. Her collaboration with broadcaster Erin Andrews gave her an opportunity to create something that was not simply connected to the Chiefs or her family."Coming out with a capsule collection with Erin was a way for me to create something that is my own," Gracie says.She explained why that distinction mattered."Obviously it's in partnership with Wear, so it's our own — but it wasn't a Chiefs project or a family initiative," she says. "It was a Gracie Hunt initiative and something that I cared about, that I spent a lot of time creating and hoping that women would love as much as I did."Her work with the Chiefs community remains important, especially the charitable efforts she experienced alongside her mother. From supporting people facing homelessness and hunger to helping build homes with Habitat for Humanity, Hunt has treated philanthropy as more than a public title.She also champions the growing influence of women in NFL fashion, pointing to designers and Chiefs WAGs who are expanding the options available to female fans.That balance may be the most interesting part of Hunt’s story. She has no need to reject her family legacy to establish herself. Instead, she is using the opportunities around her while building a career that carries her own name."I am certainly so fulfilled by all the things that I have created for myself opportunity-wise outside of football. But it's been a pleasure to be of some part of something that's greater than myself, to serve where there's room and need and to be their number one fan," she says of the Kansas City Chiefs.
Article Summary: Gracie Hunt is the daughter of Kansas City Chiefs chairman and CEO Clark Hunt and granddaughter of franchise founder Lamar Hunt. Hunt could easily have made the Chiefs her entire professional world. Instead, she has built a portfolio that reflects interests she developed long before stepping into the family spotlight.

Article Title: Career turning point: “I’m not a Serena fan. I’m just a tennis player”: How Naomi Osaka’s emotional US Open win over Serena Williams changed her career forever, making her a global star

How did beating Serena Williams become Naomi Osaka’s career turning point?

How did the 2018 US Open change Naomi Osaka’s career?

Why does Serena Williams remain central to Naomi Osaka’s career story?

Naomi Osaka arrived at the 2018 US Open as a talented 20-year-old who had already shown she could trouble the biggest names in tennis. What happened in New York, however, turned her from a rising star into a Grand Slam champion.Her 6-2, 6-4 victory over Serena Williams in the final was more than Osaka’s first major title. It became the defining moment of her career and the match that introduced her to a global audience in a way no previous result had done.The signs that Osaka was ready for a major breakthrough had already appeared earlier in 2018. She won her first WTA title at Indian Wells, beating Daria Kasatkina 6-3, 6-2 in the final after defeating Maria Sharapova, Agnieszka Radwanska, Karolina Pliskova and world No. 1 Simona Halep during the tournament. The run pushed her into the world’s top 25 and gave her the confidence to believe she could compete with the best players on the biggest stages.The US Open, though, presented a completely different challenge. Osaka entered the tournament as the No. 20 seed and reached her first Grand Slam final without dropping a set in the semifinal against Madison Keys. She beat the American 6-2, 6-4 and saved all 13 break points she faced, becoming the first Japanese woman in the Open Era to reach a Grand Slam singles final.Waiting for her was Serena, the player Osaka had admired since childhood. Osaka had never hidden what Serena meant to her. Before the final, she explained that she had dreamed about facing Williams on a Grand Slam stage since she was a child. Yet she also understood that treating the final like a fan could make the occasion overwhelming, so she tried to separate her admiration from the task in front of her.“Even when I was a little kid, I always dreamed that I would play Serena in a final of a Grand Slam,” Osaka said before the match.She then added, “At the same time I feel like even though I should enjoy this moment, I should still think of it as another match. I shouldn't really think of her as my idol. I should just try to play her as an opponent.”That approach showed immediately. Osaka played with remarkable control, breaking Serena early in the first set and refusing to allow the occasion to dictate her tennis. She won the opening set 6-2 and carried that momentum into the second.The final became increasingly tense because of the controversy surrounding Serena and chair umpire Carlos Ramos. Williams received a code violation for coaching, followed by a point penalty after breaking her racquet and a game penalty after being assessed a verbal abuse violation. The situation created a hostile atmosphere inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, but Osaka continued trying to stay focused on the match.She eventually closed it out 6-2, 6-4 on her second championship point.The credentials showed just how composed she had been. Osaka hit six aces, saved five of six break points and converted four of five break opportunities against Williams. More importantly, she never allowed the drama around the court to pull her completely away from the job.That was what made the victory such a major turning point. Osaka did not simply beat one of the greatest players in tennis. She handled the pressure of playing her childhood idol, the weight of a Grand Slam final and an increasingly emotional atmosphere, all before turning 21.After the match, Osaka famously said, “When I step onto the court, I feel like a different person. I’m not a Serena fan. I’m just a tennis player playing another tennis player. But then when I hugged her at the net, I felt like a little kid again.”That quote captured the strange reality of the night. On the court, Osaka had played Serena as an opponent. At the net, she was still the young girl who had grown up watching her.The title immediately changed Osaka’s position in tennis. Before New York, she was a promising young player with one WTA title. After New York, she was a Grand Slam champion and one of the biggest names in the sport.She also became the first Japanese player, male or female, to win a Grand Slam singles title. That achievement gave her a place in Japanese tennis history while also establishing her as one of the leading players of her generation.The victory over Serena was not an isolated success either. Osaka followed it by winning the 2019 Australian Open, where she defeated Petra Kvitova in the final. That second major title made her the first Japanese player to reach the No. 1 ranking in the WTA rankings.Her rise continued at the 2020 US Open. Osaka defeated Victoria Azarenka in the final after recovering from a set and a break down to claim her third Grand Slam title. In 2021, she won the Australian Open again, beating Jennifer Brady in the final for her fourth major championship.That sequence changed the way Osaka was viewed. The 2018 US Open was no longer simply a surprising breakthrough. It became the beginning of a period in which she established herself as a genuine Grand Slam force.Her success also gave her a much larger platform away from tennis. Osaka became one of the most recognizable athletes in the world, with her public profile growing alongside her results. Her willingness to speak openly about pressure, expectations and life away from the court also made her a prominent figure far beyond tennis.Yet the significance of the 2018 final goes deeper than the trophies that followed. It showed Osaka that she could handle a moment that looked almost impossibly large. She was facing a player she had idolized, in front of a packed New York crowd, with her first Grand Slam title within reach. Instead of allowing the occasion to overwhelm her, she trusted the tennis that had taken her there.Osaka herself later reflected on how quickly her life changed after winning Indian Wells and then the US Open. In 2026, she recalled that after Indian Wells she thought life could not get much crazier because the victory had helped her mother retire. Then the US Open brought another level of change.That progression helps explain why New York remains such an important part of her career story. Indian Wells proved Osaka could beat elite players. The US Open proved she could do it when everything around the match became enormous.Serena’s importance to Osaka’s story did not disappear after that final. If anything, the match created a connection between the two players that became part of Osaka’s identity.The most striking part was how Osaka viewed Serena even after becoming the person who had defeated her in a Grand Slam final. The result did not erase the admiration she had carried since childhood.“The thing is, I don't know what happened on the court. So for me, I'm always going to remember the Serena that I love,” Osaka said after the final. “It doesn't change anything for me.”That sentiment explained why the victory was so emotional for her. Osaka had achieved the dream she had once imagined as a young fan, but the person standing across the net was still someone she respected deeply.At the same time, Osaka understood that beating Serena meant she had to create her own identity. She later put that balance into simple words: “She’ll always be someone I look up to. But tennis-wise, I want to try to do my own thing. I want to be my own person.”That became an important theme of Osaka’s career. She was no longer simply the player who admired Serena Williams. She had become a champion with her own place in tennis.Still, when looking for the single moment that changed the direction of her career, the answer remains clear. Indian Wells announced Osaka to the tennis world, but the 2018 US Open final changed her status forever.She entered Arthur Ashe Stadium as a 20-year-old playing her childhood idol. She left it as a Grand Slam champion and the first Japanese player to win a major singles title. The controversy surrounding the final became part of its history, but Osaka’s tennis was what ultimately defined the night.Hence, the 2018 US Open remains the clearest career turning point for Naomi Osaka. It was the night she stopped being the promising young player everyone was watching and became the champion everyone had to watch.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka beat Serena Williams 6-2, 6-4 in the 2018 US Open final. It was the first Grand Slam title for the 20-year-old Japanese tennis player. The victory introduced Osaka to a global audience in a way no previous result had.

Article Title: “Prepared 500 servings for 125 local families”: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies team up with Pete’s Garden, Shelter KC and FARE for Kansas City community impact

Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ Thanksgiving partnership with Shelter KC

Patrick and Brittany Mahomes ’ charitable work through their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has addressed various needs across the Kansas City community, from food insecurity to food allergy education.Through separate partnerships with Pete’s Garden, Shelter KC, and Food Allergy Research & Education [FARE], the Foundation has wholeheartedly supported families with meals, community resources, and practical, reliable information designed to make day-to-day life safer, better, and more manageable.The initiatives emphasize that access to food involves much more than putting a meal on the table. For some families, the challenge is food insecurity. For others, specifically those managing food allergies, navigating meals safely can require valuable education, public awareness, and trustworthy support.In partnership with Pete’s Garden, the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation supported a heartfelt initiative that brought culinary education and community service together back in April 2025.At Manual Career Technical Center in the Kansas City Public School District, culinary students sincerely prepared 500 servings of Lentil Ragu over Pasta for approximately 125 local families served by Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City.“When students realize they can cook a meal that feeds a community, something changes,” said Tamara Weber, Founder and Executive Director of Pete’s Garden.“By equipping educators with the tools and resources to lead impactful service projects, we’re building a movement of young leaders who understand the power of food to create change.”The insightful effort was part of Pete’s Garden’s Kids Feeding Kids program, which provides high school students with real-world, hands-on experience planning, preparing, and packaging family-sized meals.The service-learning opportunity also familiarizes students with serious issues surrounding food insecurity and food access within their own communities.Kids Feeding Kids program was launched in 2021 with funding from Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.The program grew from one pilot school to 35 participating schools across Kansas and Missouri for the 2024-2025 school year.The sagacious collaboration generated a dual impact: families received prepared meals, while young culinary students grasped real-world experience and a rare opportunity to use their developing skills in service of others.“Sitting down as a family to a healthy and wholesome meal is something Brittany and I really value,” said Patrick Mahomes “But too many Kansas City families are struggling to get a wholesome dinner on the table. We are proud to support Kids Feeding Kids and help make mealtime easier for these families while also engaging students in a meaningful community service experience.”For 75 years, Shelter KC has been a haven for Kansas City’s homeless men and women. In November 2024, Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies Foundation worked with them to support Kansas City families dealing with hardship during the holiday season.The Foundation made a $15,000 donation to support Shelter KC’s annual Thanksgiving Family Feast.The contribution was wholeheartedly intended to provide Thanksgiving dinners for over 200 Kansas City families in need.Shelter KC and Foundation volunteers were scheduled to prepare meal boxes and help create a celebration day centered on food preparation, building connection, and community service.The Thanksgiving partnership mirrored the Foundation’s comprehensive commitment to supporting children and families through initiatives concentrated on health, wellness, and community resources, while also helping extend Shelter KC’s reach during the festive time of year. When nobody deserves to be sad or in need of wholesome food.“We are incredibly grateful to 15 and the Mahomies Foundation for this support,” said Shelter KC Executive Director Eric Burger.“Their partnership is an inspiring reminder that we are all part of the same community, responsible for lifting one another up.This donation ensures that families who may be struggling this holiday season will have a Thanksgiving meal to enjoy together, and a renewed sense of hope for the future.”Food-related support has also become a crucial portion of the Foundation’s work through its partnership with FARE [Food Allergy Research & Education]. The joint initiative, known as “15 and FARE,” was established to expand food allergy education, support, and resources throughout the Kansas City area.On July 18, 2026, from 1 to 4 PM, “15 and FARE” hosted a free Back-to-School event at the Kansas City Public Library’s Plaza Branch for Kansas City-area families managing food allergies.The afternoon-held event included a Top 9 allergen-free school lunch demonstration, an Ask-the-Expert panel, a kids’ fun zone, and other health resources.The free open-to-the-public event was designed to help families prepare for the new school year while addressing questions that can arise when children with food allergies return to cafeteria lunches, classroom activities, field trips, and extracurricular programs where their parents or caregivers are not by their side.“As a food allergy mom myself, I know how important it is for families to feel prepared and supported, especially during back-to-school season,” said Brittany Mahomes, food allergy advocate and 15 and the Mahomies co-founder.“For parents managing food allergies, having access to trusted resources and a strong community can make all the difference.15 and the Mahomies is proud to partner with FARE to bring Kansas City families together for a day of learning, connection, and fun.”
Article Summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes ’ charitable work through their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has addressed various needs across the Kansas City community. The Foundation has wholeheartedly supported families with meals, community resources, and practical, reliable information designed to make day-to-day life safer, better and more manageable.

Article Title: “My cup for myself was half empty”: How LeBron James’ wife Savannah James rediscovered herself after motherhood and built a life beyond raising her three children

Everybody’s Crazy

A new chapter took shape as Savannah James built a life beyond motherhood

Savannah James spent much of her adult life putting family first. She became a mother at 18 and eventually raised three children while LeBron James built a historic NBA career. Yet behind the polished family image, Savannah has admitted that she struggled with her own identity. Years of being a mother and wife had left little room to ask a simple question: who was Savannah outside those roles?That question became harder to ignore as the children grew older. Savannah eventually started taking time for herself and exploring interests beyond family life. What followed was a gradual shift that brought new projects, business ventures and a better understanding of what she needed personally.Savannah James welcomed Bronny James in October 2004, followed by Bryce in June 2007 and Zhuri in October 2014. With three children at different stages of life and LeBron James constantly balancing an NBA schedule, much of Savannah’s attention naturally went toward her family.Still, Savannah later acknowledged that the balance had become difficult. During a 2025 episode of, the podcast Savannah co-hosts with April McDaniel, she spoke openly about feeling disconnected from the person she had been before motherhood. “It wasn’t just my kids, it was my husband, I felt like I didn’t have an identity outside of that,” Savannah said during the podcast.She also explained how much of her energy went into being a mother.“I was too wrapped up in just being their mom,” Savannah said in the same conversation. That realization forced her to look beyond the responsibilities that had defined much of her life.Savannah described the feeling in even more personal terms during the 2025 podcast discussion. “My cup for myself was half empty,” she said.The answer was not to step away from her children or marriage. Instead, Savannah began creating small pockets of time that belonged only to her. She recalled taking solo weekend trips while living in Ohio and learning to become more protective of her schedule.“I hate to say it like this, but just be selfish with my time,” Savannah said on Everybody’s Crazy in 2025. She also explained that she needed to discover who she was outside of Bronny and Bryce. That process had roots several years earlier.Savannah had already discussed the emotional weight of balancing family and personal needs before that 2025 conversation. In a June 21, 2024 interview with “Harper’s Bazaar”, she talked about creatingwith April McDaniel, a platform focused on women, personal growth and self-discovery.The idea connected directly to Savannah’s own experience. She wanted women to have space to slow down and think about themselves instead of constantly meeting everyone else’s needs.“If I’m working from a glass half empty, I’m not good to anybody,” Savannah said on June 21, 2024.That mindset also shaped the way Savannah approached motherhood as her children became more independent. Bronny moved into college basketball, Bryce continued developing his own basketball career, and Zhuri grew into her own interests. Savannah suddenly had more room to explore what came next.She used that space to build a public identity separate from LeBron James. Alongside “Everybody’s Crazy”, Savannah developed business ventures and continued working on projects connected to wellness, lifestyle and personal growth. In 2025, she also launched Reframe, a skincare brand that added another piece to her growing business portfolio.The change did not mean Savannah stopped being a mother. It meant motherhood no longer had to be the only role defining her. After years of giving most of her energy to LeBron James and their three children, Savannah began treating her own ambitions as something worth protecting too. Her journey shows a quieter side of family life that rarely appears in the spotlight: sometimes finding yourself starts with simply making enough room to hear your own thoughts again.

She became a mother at 18 and eventually raised three children while LeBron James built a historic NBA career. After years of giving most of her energy to LeBron James and their three children, Savannah began treating her ambitions as something too.

No credible sources report any such change.”That does not, by itself, prove that the images were created with AI. Still, it gives an important reason not to treat the plastic-surgery claim as fact. The “#ad” label also raises questions about the purpose of the post. There has been no clear explanation of what the advertisement was for.The unusual images also led to comments from people who believed Matthews had changed his appearance. One person wrote, “Clay Matthews got reconstructive surgery to look like the gigachad meme 😭,” while another said, “You won’t believe how much he spent just to look this.” A third person added, “This can’t be real,” showing that some viewers were already questioning whether the pictures were genuine.The timing of the photos is another reason the claim needs caution. The episode featured him discussing his work with Netflix, the Rams-49ers game in Australia and his life after football.Matthews also appeared on Bussin’ With The Boys on September 3 alongside Will Compton, Taylor Lewan and Delanie Walker. T20I career so far

Abhishek Sharma has come a long way from the little boy in Amritsar who first picked up a cricket bat at the age of three-and-a-half. On his birthday, his journey stands out as one of the most remarkable rises in modern T20 cricket, from a promising youngster in Punjab to an India regular and the holder of the highest-ever ICC T20I batting rating.Abhishek's father, Raj Kumar Sharma, a former cricketer, introduced him to the game when he was just three-and-a-half. The youngster quickly developed an obsession with batting and progressed through Punjab's age-group system.His numbers soon began attracting attention. During the 2015-16 Vijay Merchant Trophy, Abhishek scored more than 1,200 runs at an average of 109.09 and also claimed 57 wickets. He captained Punjab to the Under-19 Asia Cup title in 2016 before becoming part of India's victorious Under-19 World Cup campaign in 2018.The IPL came at just 17, when Delhi Daredevils picked him in the 2018 auction. His career, however, did not explode immediately. Abhishek spent several seasons developing his game through domestic cricket and the IPL before finding the perfect platform for his aggressive style.A major influence during that period was Yuvraj Singh. The former India all-rounder became Abhishek's mentor and worked closely with him, particularly during the Covid-19 lockdown.Yuvraj understood the youngster's attacking instincts and encouraged him to embrace them rather than become overly cautious. That philosophy eventually became the foundation of Abhishek's T20 game.His international breakthrough came after making his T20I debut in July 2024. In February 2025, Abhishek produced one of the most devastating T20I innings by an Indian batter when he smashed 135 off just 54 balls against England in Mumbai. The innings contained 13 sixes and a 37-ball century, announcing him as one of India's most dangerous T20 batters.The 135 was only the beginning. During the 2025 Asia Cup, Abhishek established himself as India's attacking force at the top of the order. He scored 314 runs in seven matches at a strike rate of 200 and was named Player of the Tournament as India won the competition.His performances pushed him to the top of the ICC T20I batting rankings and eventually into record-breaking territory. After scoring 61 against Sri Lanka, Abhishek reached 931 rating points, the highest-ever rating achieved by a men's T20I batter.He surpassed Dawid Malan's previous record of 919 and moved beyond the best ratings achieved by India's Suryakumar Yadav and Virat Kohli.The numbers behind Abhishek's rise were extraordinary. In 2025, he became the first player to score more than 1,000 runs in T20 cricket in a calendar year while maintaining a strike rate above 200. He finished the year at a strike rate of 202 and smashed 108 sixes.His IPL performances were equally destructive. Playing for Sunrisers Hyderabad, Abhishek produced a stunning 141 off 55 balls against Punjab Kings in IPL 2025. He reached his fifty in only 16 balls and his century in 40, hitting 14 fours and 10 sixes as Hyderabad chased down 246. The innings broke KL Rahul's record for the highest score by an Indian batter in IPL history.His development has been shaped by several influential figures. Apart from Yuvraj, Abhishek has drawn lessons from players such as Shikhar Dhawan, Brian Lara and Travis Head. At Sunrisers, his partnership with Head showed how effectively his aggressive approach could work against the best bowling attacks.At the 2026 T20 World Cup, Abhishek added another major achievement to his growing list, playing a crucial role in India's title-winning campaign, including a blistering 52 off 21 balls in the final against New Zealand.Abhishek Sharma has played 56 T20Is between 2024 and 2026, scoring 1,629 runs in 55 innings at an average of 30.73 and a remarkable strike rate of 187.24. He has registered two centuries and 11 fifties, with a highest score of 135. His aggressive approach is reflected in his boundary count, with the left-hander hitting 164 fours and 104 sixes in his international career so far.
